subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work PB89, then kb/Work PB153, then kb/Work PB450 half 2 (wave 43 group D/E). SR19 IS THREE SENTENCES, AND THE ROW NAMED A WITNESS FOR ONLY THE FIRST. PB89 landed sentence 1's TO NULL arm ('identifier-6 shall be the predefined address NULL or shall reference a data-pointer' - it had been a parse error) and the row's single test-ref, conformance:cases/13.18.38-OCCURS/pb80_based_odo_group, exercises exactly that and nothing else; sentences 2 and 3 are the restricted-data-pointer screens, which PB153 landed with two negatives the row never named. This record adds them. ### SENTENCE 3 IS NOT SR20. The converse sentence ('If identifier-6 references a restricted data-pointer, either identifier-5 shall reference a data-pointer restricted to the same type or data-name-1 shall be a typed item of the type to which identifier-6 is restricted' - cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 OK, returned as 19)) is an UNNUMBERED continuation paragraph of rule 19; RENDERED at 300 dpi from the printed page (folio 736 / PDF p766), 20) is FORMAT 8's 'Identifier-12 shall reference a data item of category function-pointer ...'. Six code sites and two goldens carried the inherited SR20, including the user-visible COBOL0869 message; all are corrected. ### AND PB450 OPENED A CELL SENTENCE 3 COULD NOT REACH. Until Format 7's receiving operand became the printed repeated brace, identifier-6's restriction reached the screen only through an `ADDRESS OF x` sender (Annex D.9.2.2 source 2, 8.4.3.11.4 GR2), because the two fixed productions split on the SENDER's spelling meant a PLAIN restricted pointer item could never stand as identifier-6 beside an ADDRESS OF receiver - MEASURED before the landing, `SET ADDRESS OF B1 P-PLAIN TO P-RESTRICTED` was `error COBOL0001: unexpected 'P-PLAIN'`. It is now screened from D.9.2.2 source 1 as well (13.18.60.4 GR23, 'If type-name-1 is specified, this data item is a restricted data-pointer' - cite.py --check OK), and negative/pb450-set-format7-restricted-sender-second-receiver pins it at the SECOND receiving operand with the first one conforming, so the case cannot pass for the wrong reason. Both SR19 screens are asked PER RECEIVING OPERAND (ScreenPointerReceiverRestriction), because the restriction is the operand's and not the statement's.
